title: WPSS/966/2022 of PRABHA DEVI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 966 of 2022
Prabha Devi ........Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ........Respondents
Present:-
Heard Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for the petitioner, Mr. Sachin Mohan
Singh Mehta, Brief Holder for the State and Mr. Prem Kaushal, Advocate
for the respondent Corporation.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
The petitioner has challenged the order dated 02.06.2020 issued
by the respondent no. 2, whereby, the representation of the petitioners
husband disentitling him for the 3rd ACP was rejected and further the
order dated 27.01.2022 issued by the respondent no. 2, whereby, the
re-fixation of the salary of the husband of the petitioner was done, and
after re-fixation of the salary, amount of retiral dues under the ACP,
the gratuity was reduced from Rs. 7,67,340/- to Rs. 4,61,851/- as well
as the order dated 18.06.2021, whereby, the 2nd ACP was also
withdrawn after his retirement.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that the husband of the petitioner
was working with the respondent Transport Corporation as Driver in
Ramnagar Depot and he retired from such post on 29.02.2020 after
superannuation. After retirement of the petitioner, retiral dues
including gratuity, etc. of Rs. 7,67,340/- was sanctioned in favour of
the husband of the petitioner, but, subsequently, the said order was
refixed/amended on the ground that the pay/ACP of the petitioner was
amended vide order no. 0788 dated 18.06.2021 and order dated 0789
dated 18.06.2021, whereby, the ACP and salary of the petitioner were
amended respectively and consequently the amount of gratuity was
reduced to Rs. 4,61,851/-.

2
3. It is also the case of the petitioner that petitioner was entitled to
get the 3rd ACP after completion of 26 years of service w.e.f. 2016,
but, the same has not been sanctioned and paid to the petitioner. It is
contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the salary has
been refixed by the respondent department of the petitioner's husband
after his retirement and that too after a period of ten years of fixation
of salary and payment of 2nd ACP, such pay-fixation cannot be done
by the respondent department. It is further submitted by the learned
counsel for the petitioner that it is not the case of the respondent-Corporation that at any point of time, the husband of the petitioner was
instrumental in getting any wrong fixation of such salary and for no
reason, the same has been re-fixed and consequently, the gratuity was
reduced and 3rd ACP has also not been paid.
4. The respondent-Corporation has filed its counter affidavit and in
counter affidavit, it has been mainly contended by the respondent
Corporation in paragraph 4 and 5, it is quoted below:-
4. That the husband of petitioner Sri Rajesh Tyagi was appointed on
12.10.1990 on the post of Driver. During his service in the character roll of
Sri Rajesh Tyagi adverse entries were recorded for 1991-92, 1994-95,
1995-96, 1996-97, 1997-98, 1998-99, 2003-04 and as such his services
were not satisfactory. He had been awarded the following punishment.
1. Vide order dated 27.4.96 he was suspended and consequently vide
order dated 02.7.98 he was tentatively reinstated in service
2. Vide order dated 19.8.2002 the annual increment of two years with
cumulative effect was stopped he was reinstated in service by recording
adverse entry in character roll.
3. Vide order dated 31.3.03 the remaining salary of suspension period was
forfeited and increment of 02 years was stopped.
4. Vide order dated 8.6.04 he was suspended.
5. Vide order dated 29.11.04 he was reinstated by keeping him in basic
initial pay scale of 3050 for 03 years and was posted in Rudrapur Depot.
5. That the above punishment order reveals that the service of petitioner's
husband was not satisfactory. As per the G.O. no. 872 dated 8.3.2011 as
amended by GO no. 313 dated 30.10.2012 and GO no. 589 dated 1.7.2013,
on completion of 10, 16 and 26 years of satisfactory and unblemished
services the 1st 2nd and 3rd ACP is granted. Furthermore in Clause 6 of the

3
Circular no. 164 dated 11.11.2020 of the Transport Corporation
Headquarter, if during the applicability of ACP the incumbent has been
punished by placing in lower scale of his post or in 1 stage of the pay, then
for the purpose of ACP the service of further years will be counted. It is
provided in Clause 7 of the circular that if at the time of applicability of
ACP, if the annual increment of an employee for one or more year has been
stopped with cumulative effect then the applicability of ACP will be
counted from double of the said punishment year.
On account of unsatisfactory service of Sri Rajesh Tyagi and from
29.11.04 placing him on the initial pay scale, the ACP was counted after
further three years i.e. 29.11.2007 but due to unsatisfactory annual
confidential report of year 2016-17 the Assistant General Manager,
Ramangar vide order dated 18.6.2021 cancelled the earlier granted 2nd
ACP grade pay 2800 w.e.f. 1.9.10 and on the basis of MACPS granted
financial upgradation grade pay 2000 (pay matrix level3) .w.e.f 29.11.2018
and on the basis of that order the earlier issued gratuity order dated
29.2.2020 was amended and order dated 23.6.2021 for payment of
amended gratuity. True copy of Circular no. 164 dated 11.11.2020 is
annexed as Annexure CA-3 to this affidavit.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Corporation
that husband of the petitioner Late Shri Rajesh Tyagi was awarded
various adverse entries in the year 1991-1992, 1994-95, 1995-96,
1996-97, 1997-98, 1998-99, 1999-2000 and 2003-2004 and for that
reason, his services were not satisfactory and he was awarded certain
punishments quoted in paragraph-4 of the counter affidavit. It is
submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation that
due to these punishments, it cannot be said that the service of the
husband of the petitioner was satisfactory and since Government
Order, which provides for the payment of 1st, 2nd and 3rd ACP
prescribes that the ACP can only be admissible to such employees of
the respondent-Corporation, who have unblemished and satisfactory
service to their credit. Since, the service of the husband of the
petitioner was not unblemished, therefore, the ACP, which was
granted to him, was withdrawn and accordingly, the pay was re-fixed.

4
6. It is admitted fact that when the 2nd ACP was granted to the
husband of the petitioner on 01.09.2010, the entire service record of
the husband of the petitioner was before the Corporation and having
paid/sanctioned the 1st and 2nd ACP to the husband of the petitioner,
there was no occasion for the respondent-Corporation to re-visit the
same and to withdraw that and to re-fix the salary of the husband of
the petitioner. There is yet another aspect of the matter that by
sanctioning the ACP to the husband of the petitioner, certain financial
rights have accrued in his favour and the same cannot be withdrawn
without providing any opportunity to the husband of the petitioner,
but, in the case in hand, the said exercise was done by the respondent-Corporation even after retirement of the husband of the petitioner in
the year 2020, and while he was battling cancer, he died on
26.10.2021. His salary was re-fixed and ACP was withdrawn on
18.06.2021. This kind of exercise of power is highly arbitrary and
illegal and cannot sustain in the eyes of law.
7. Accordingly, the order impugned in the writ petition so far as by
which the ACP was withdrawn and the salary was re-fixed by the
respondent-Corporation are hereby quashed and the order by which the
gratuity was reduced from Rs. 7,67,340/- to Rs. 4,61,851/- is also
hereby quashed. So far as the denial of 3rd ACP is concerned, since, the
decision thereon has not been taken by the respondent-Corporation, the
same cannot be found faulted with for the reason that the husband of
the petitioner was not having an unblemished service career and for
that, the respondent department is free to pass any order as per the
Government Order. The respondent-Corporation is directed to pay
back the dues as admissible to the petitioner within six weeks from
today.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition stands partly allowed with the
above observations.
9. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed-off accordingly.

5
10. No orders as to cost.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 18.12.2023
Ujjwal
